# Data Processing Agreement (DPA)

## Article 28 GDPR

**Between:**

**The Client** (the "**Controller**" or "Client"), identified per its account registration details,

**And:**

**Sealmetrics S.L.**, Spanish tax ID ESB70933239, registered office at Carrer de Tirso de Molina 36, 08940 Cornellà de Llobregat, Barcelona, Spain (the "**Processor**" or "Sealmetrics").

**Effective date:** the date of acceptance of the Sealmetrics Terms of Service, which incorporate this DPA by reference.

**Reference:** DPA-2026-v2.2 (EN). The Spanish version is the authoritative text; this English version is provided for convenience.

---

## RECITALS

I. The Client has engaged Sealmetrics' audience measurement and web analytics service under the Terms of Service.

II. In providing the service, Sealmetrics processes, on the Client's behalf, data relating to visitors of the Client's websites, which qualify as **pseudonymised personal data** (not anonymous data). The service is built on data protection by design and by default (Art. 25 GDPR): no cookies or terminal-equipment storage, no persistence of IP addresses in the analytics database, and a pseudonymised, ephemeral session identifier that is unfit for tracking across sites or across days.

III. The parties formalise this processing arrangement under Art. 28 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 ("GDPR"), the Spanish LOPDGDD (LO 3/2018) and the criteria of the AEPD Guide on the use of cookies for audience measurement tools (January 2024).

IV. This DPA forms an integral part of the Terms of Service and **prevails** over any conflicting provision therein regarding data protection.

---

## CLAUSES

### 1. DEFINITIONS

"Personal data", "processing", "controller", "processor", "personal data breach" and "supervisory authority" have the meaning given in Art. 4 GDPR. In addition:

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| **Service** | The Sealmetrics web analytics platform described in the Terms of Service |
| **Service Data** | The data processed on the Client's behalf as described in **Annex 1** |
| **Sub-processor** | A third party engaged by Sealmetrics that processes Service Data |
| **Data Subjects** | Visitors of the Client's websites where the Service is integrated |
| **BYOK** | "Bring Your Own Key": optional configuration whereby the Client connects its own API key of an external AI provider |
| **SCCs** | Standard Contractual Clauses under Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/914 |

### 2. SUBJECT MATTER, NATURE AND SCOPE

2.1. This Agreement governs the processing of Service Data that Sealmetrics carries out **on behalf of and under the documented instructions of the Client**, with the subject matter, duration, nature, purpose, data types and categories of data subjects described in **Annex 1**.

2.2. **Documented instructions.** The Client's complete documented instructions consist of: (i) this DPA and its Annex 1; (ii) the Terms of Service; and (iii) the configuration the Client applies in the platform (conversion events, properties, integrations, exports). Sealmetrics shall not process Service Data for any other purpose.

2.3. Sealmetrics shall promptly inform the Client if, in its view, an instruction infringes the GDPR or other applicable data protection law, and may suspend its execution until clarified.

### 3. SPECIFIC AUDIENCE-MEASUREMENT GUARANTEES (AEPD criteria)

In compliance with the contractual guarantees that the AEPD audience-measurement guide (January 2024, section III.C) requires of the provider, Sealmetrics undertakes towards the Client:

3.1. **No reuse.** Not to reuse Service Data for any purpose of its own or of third parties: no model training, no algorithm improvement using identifiable data, no cross-client benchmarking, no disclosure or sale. Service Data is processed in the Client's name exclusively.

3.2. **Purpose restriction.** To limit processing to: (a) the strictly necessary audience measurements listed by the AEPD (page-by-page audience; referrers; device, browser and screen type; interaction times and rates; user actions; country-level geographic area); and (b) the marketing-attribution features (conversions, amounts, ad network type of the click and conversion properties) **expressly instructed by the Client** through its configuration, whose legal basis it is for the Client, as controller, to document (clause 5.4).

3.3. **Multi-publisher independence.** To collect, process and store Service Data **independently for each client**, with per-account logical isolation across all storage layers, and to use technical identifiers that are independent per client and unfit for cross-referencing, profile duplication or unified reach measurement across sites of different controllers.

3.4. **Location.** To process Service Data entirely within the European Union (clause 7).

3.5. **Documented assessment.** To keep at the Client's disposal a documented assessment of the Service's configuration against the requirements of the said guide (section III.C.2), updated at least annually, which the Client may request for its own compliance records.

3.6. **Transparency: model notice and changes to the processing** (Art. 28.3.f GDPR). To assist the Client with its information duties (Arts. 12-14 GDPR), Sealmetrics undertakes to:

a) **Accurate model notice.** Keep published, and available in the dashboard, a versioned model notice for Data Subjects that accurately describes the processing carried out by the Service according to each site's configuration (blocks per enabled feature). Sealmetrics is responsible for the **technical accuracy** of that description. Its legal adaptation, the choice of legal basis and its publication are the Client's responsibility (clause 5.1).

b) **Notice of changes.** Notify the Client, by email to the account and in the dashboard, of any change to the processing that affects the information to be provided to Data Subjects, together with the new version of the model notice:
   - at least **30 days** before the change applies;
   - unless the change reduces the processing or is required for legal or security reasons, in which case notice will be given without delay.

c) **Contextual information.** Display the corresponding information block when the Client enables a feature that requires it (conversion attribution, eCommerce integrations, automated-traffic detection, AI, exports).

d) **Record of confirmations.** Keep a record of the Client's confirmations under clause 5.1.c: user, date, site, version of the notice and features enabled at that time. The record will be provided to the Client upon request.

### 4. PROCESSOR OBLIGATIONS

#### 4.1. Confidentiality
Persons authorised to process Service Data are bound by contractual confidentiality undertakings that survive the end of their engagement with Sealmetrics. Access follows the least-privilege principle and is logged.

#### 4.2. Security (Art. 32)
Sealmetrics implements and maintains the technical and organisational measures of **Annex 2**, appropriate to the risk, including encryption in transit and of application secrets at rest, structural minimisation (no IPs persisted in the analytics database, no terminal-equipment storage), automatically enforced retention periods, per-account isolation and incident management. Measures may be updated provided the level of protection is not reduced.

#### 4.3. Sub-processors
a) The Client grants **general authorisation** for the sub-processors in **Annex 3**, published and maintained in Sealmetrics' sub-processor list.
b) Sealmetrics shall give notice of additions or replacements **reasonably in advance so that the Client can exercise its right to object** (via the public list and/or account email). The Client may object on reasonable data protection grounds; failing an agreed solution, it may terminate the affected Service without penalty.
c) Sealmetrics shall impose on each sub-processor, by contract, obligations equivalent to those of this DPA, and remains liable to the Client for its sub-processors' compliance.
d) **Providers connected by the Client are not Sealmetrics sub-processors**: AI providers configured under BYOK and export destinations chosen by the Client (clause 6) act upon the Client's direct designation.

#### 4.4. Assistance with data subjects' rights (Arts. 11 and 12-22)
a) Due to the nature of the Service, Sealmetrics **has no means of identifying Data Subjects** from Service Data: no direct identifiers exist, IPs are not persisted in the analytics database, and the session identifier is an ephemeral pseudonym. **Art. 11 GDPR** applies. If the Client receives a rights request from a visitor, Sealmetrics will assist by:
   - providing the description of the processing;
   - confirming that identification is, as a general matter, not possible;
   - where the data subject provides additional information that appears in Service Data (for example, a value sent by the Client as a conversion property), searching for and, where applicable, deleting the corresponding records.
b) Sealmetrics shall forward to the Client **without undue delay** any request received directly from a Data Subject, and shall not respond to it except on the Client's instruction.
c) Sealmetrics shall carry out the deletion of an account's Service Data upon the Client's instruction (clause 4.8).

#### 4.5. Personal data breaches (Arts. 33-34)
a) Sealmetrics shall notify the Client **without undue delay** after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting Service Data (the wording of Art. 33.2 GDPR), mindful of the 72-hour period available to the Client vis-à-vis the supervisory authority.
b) The notification shall include, where available: the nature of the breach, the categories and approximate volume of data subjects and records concerned, the likely consequences, the measures taken or proposed, and a contact point. Information may be provided in phases.
c) Sealmetrics shall cooperate with the Client's notification and communication obligations and shall internally document every breach in accordance with Art. 33.5.

#### 4.6. Assistance with DPIAs and prior consultation (Arts. 35-36)
Sealmetrics shall assist the Client, taking into account the information available to it, with data protection impact assessments and prior consultations concerning the Service, and keeps technical documentation of the processing (architecture, data inventory, retention periods, the AEPD assessment of clause 3.5) at the Client's disposal.

#### 4.7. Information and audits (Art. 28.3.h)
a) Sealmetrics shall make available to the Client the information necessary to demonstrate compliance with this DPA, including the documentation of clause 4.6.
b) The Client (or an independent auditor that is not a Sealmetrics competitor, bound by confidentiality) may conduct audits, including inspections, with at least **30 days'** notice, at most once per 12-month period save in the event of a breach or a supervisory authority requirement, during business hours and without disproportionate interference. Each party bears its own costs; if the audit reveals a material breach, Sealmetrics shall bear the reasonable costs.

#### 4.8. End of processing (Art. 28.3.g)
a) Upon termination of the Service, the Client has **30 days** to export its data (API and/or BigQuery integration).
b) At the Client's choice, Sealmetrics shall delete or return the Service Data and delete existing copies **within a reasonable period** after the export window, unless legal retention obligations apply, in which case the data will be blocked.
c) The automatic retention periods of Annex 1 continue to apply during the life of the Service.

### 5. CONTROLLER OBLIGATIONS

5.1. **Lawfulness and information to Data Subjects.** Ensure the lawfulness of the commissioned processing, hold the applicable legal basis and comply with its information duties towards Data Subjects (Arts. 12-14 GDPR). In particular, the Client undertakes to:

a) Include in the privacy policy of each site where it installs the Service information that faithfully reflects the processing described in Annex 1 and in the model notice of clause 3.6, including the blocks for the features it has enabled. It must do so before installing the Service or, for sites where the Service is already installed, within 30 days of the entry into force of this version of the DPA. In particular, it shall not describe the data processed by the Service as "anonymous".

b) Update that information within **30 days** of Sealmetrics notifying it of a change under clause 3.6.b, or before enabling a feature that requires an additional block.

c) Confirm in the dashboard, through a user authorised to do so, that it has carried out the actions in points a) and b). The confirmation is a **statement by the Client** and is recorded under clause 3.6.d. Failure to confirm does not release the Client from its obligation nor shift to Sealmetrics responsibility for the information duty.

5.2. **No personal data instrumentation**: the Client shall not send direct personal data to the Service through free-configuration fields — conversion properties, URL parameters, campaign names or similar (e.g. emails, phone numbers, ID numbers). Sealmetrics may apply technical detection and redaction filters as an additional safeguard, without this releasing the Client from this obligation. Data introduced in breach of this clause will be treated as Service Data for security purposes, but the Client is responsible for its lawfulness.

5.3. Configure the Service in line with its own obligations, including the decision to enable conversions, properties, eCommerce integrations, exports, BYOK or automated-traffic detection features. Automated-traffic detection (Purpose C of Annex 1) **shall only be enabled upon the Client's express and documented instruction**, given in the platform or in writing. Sealmetrics shall not enable it on its own initiative.

5.4. Document, as controller, the legal basis for the marketing-attribution layer when enabled (clause 3.2.b), with supporting documentation provided by Sealmetrics.

5.5. Handle Data Subjects' rights requests and notify Sealmetrics of changes affecting the processing.

### 6. CLIENT-DIRECTED SERVICES (BYOK, exports, webhooks)

6.1. **BYOK.** If the Client configures its own key of an external AI provider, the corresponding prompts are sent to that provider **on the Client's behalf and responsibility**, under the terms and transfer safeguards the Client holds with that provider. Sealmetrics acts as a mere conduit and is not responsible for that provider. The default provider ("Seal AI") requires no configuration and runs entirely in the EU (Annex 3).

6.2. **Exports and webhooks.** Data exported to the Client's infrastructure (API, BigQuery, webhooks, reports) is, from receipt, the Client's own processing under its exclusive responsibility, including any international transfer the destination entails.

### 7. LOCATION AND INTERNATIONAL TRANSFERS

7.1. **General rule: no transfers in the analytics flow.** Data of the Client's website visitors is processed and stored **exclusively within the European Union**, including the default AI inference (Scaleway, Paris, with zero data retention). That flow does not depend on the EU-US Data Privacy Framework or on SCCs. Sole exception in Annex 3: service emails (verifications, alerts, reports with aggregated metrics) to the Client's account users via Resend, Inc. (USA), covered by SCCs/DPF — with no effect on any visitor data.

7.2. Should a sub-processor in the future need to process Service Data outside the EEA, Sealmetrics shall: (i) give notice per clause 4.3.b; (ii) ensure a valid Chapter V instrument (adequacy decision or SCCs with supplementary measures, per **Annex 4**); and (iii) carry out and document a transfer impact assessment.

7.3. Transfers arising from Client-directed services (clause 6) are the Client's responsibility.

### 8. LIABILITY

8.1. **Statutory allocation.** Each party is liable under Art. 82 GDPR: Sealmetrics, only where it breaches GDPR obligations specifically directed at processors or acts outside the Client's lawful instructions; the Client, in all other cases (including the lawfulness of the legal basis, information duties and any data instrumented in breach of clause 5.2).

8.2. **No additional indemnities.** Neither party assumes indemnification obligations towards the other beyond those mandatorily arising from law. To the maximum extent permitted, loss of profit, loss of business, loss of the Client's own data and any indirect or consequential damages are excluded.

8.3. **Sole remedy.** To the maximum extent permitted by law, the Client's **sole remedy** against Sealmetrics for breaches of this DPA consists of **credits against or waiver of future Service fees**, up to an aggregate maximum equivalent to the fees of the 12 months preceding the triggering event. **In no event shall amounts already paid be refunded, nor shall Sealmetrics make any monetary payment.**

8.4. **Mandatory limits.** The above limitations do not apply where the law does not permit them: liability for wilful misconduct or gross negligence (Art. 1102 of the Spanish Civil Code), Data Subjects' claims under Art. 82 GDPR, and fines imposed on each party by a supervisory authority for its own non-compliance — risks that no agreement between the parties can exclude.

### 9. TERM, AMENDMENT, LAW AND JURISDICTION

9.1. This DPA applies from acceptance of the Terms and for as long as Sealmetrics processes Service Data; clauses 4.1 and 4.8 survive termination.

9.2. Amendments to this DPA will be notified reasonably in advance; Annexes 2 and 3 may be updated per their own mechanisms (4.2 and 4.3).

9.3. This Agreement is governed by **Spanish law**. The parties submit to the courts of **Barcelona**, save where mandatory rules provide otherwise. Reference supervisory authority of the Processor: **Agencia Española de Protección de Datos (AEPD)**.

### 10. NOTICES

- **Sealmetrics** — privacy@sealmetrics.com · Carrer de Tirso de Molina 36, 08940 Cornellà de Llobregat, Barcelona.
- **Client** — the email and address registered on its account.

## ANNEX 1 — DESCRIPTION OF PROCESSING (Art. 28.3 GDPR)

### A1.1 Subject matter, nature and purpose

| Aspect | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| **Subject matter** | Audience measurement and web analytics for the Client's websites |
| **Nature** | Collection via JavaScript pixel, transport, statistical aggregation, storage with automatic retention, visualisation, AI insights over aggregated data, export |
| **Purpose A — Audience measurement** | Aggregated audience and performance statistics (the strictly necessary measurements of the AEPD guide) |
| **Purpose B — Attribution (optional, per Client configuration)** | Conversions, amounts, ad network type of the campaign click (the click identifier value is not stored) and Client-defined conversion properties. In the Shopify integration, this includes associating the session identifier with the cart and the order in order to attribute the purchase |
| **Purpose C — Automated-traffic detection (optional, only upon the Client's express instruction)** | Classification of each visit as human or automated (bots, automated browsers, AI agents) to preserve the integrity of the statistics, based on additional technical browser signals, interaction patterns and network data transiently derived from the IP |
| **Duration** | The life of the Service, with the retention periods of A1.4 |

### A1.2 Categories of data subjects and data

**Data subjects**: visitors of the Client's websites.

| Category | Data | Relevant detail |
|----------|------|-----------------|
| Browsing | URL visited, referrer, landing page, events, duration/engagement | URLs may contain Client-defined parameters (see clause 5.2) |
| Technical | Device type, browser, operating system (derived from the user agent), browser time zone | **The raw user agent is not retained** (derivatives only); the event-level technical log is kept for 1 day |
| IP address | Received with each request | Transient use for abuse filtering (and, under Purpose C, to derive country and network). **Not stored in the analytics database.** It may remain in internal processing queues until consumed and, if processing fails, in retry queues for up to 7 days. Removal of the IP from this transport is in progress |
| Location | **Country derived from the browser time zone** (not from the IP). On accounts with agent detection enabled, an additional IP-derived country is used transiently as an anti-fraud signal, without persisting the IP | |
| Technical identifier | Ephemeral session identifier, computed in the browser from technical characteristics **read from the terminal equipment** (e.g. browser, languages, time zone, screen, device capabilities), **with no device storage** (no cookies, no storage APIs) and independent per client. It is **pseudonymized server-side** (HMAC with a secret key and a daily salt destroyed on rotation) before any use or storage | It is pseudonymised personal data. Maximum effective life: 2 h in active session and 1 day in the technical log; not linkable across days or across sites. **Shopify integration exception:** to attribute the purchase, the identifier computed in the browser is added to the cart attributes and becomes associated with the order in the Client's store |
| Automated-traffic detection (Purpose C only) | Additional technical browser signals (e.g. WebGL, canvas, plugins, window dimensions, presence of automation tools), interaction patterns (mouse movement, scrolling, clicks), country and network provider derived from the IP | Only on sites where the Client has enabled the feature; used exclusively for the human/automated classification |
| Origin | Source/medium/campaign (UTM), **ad network type of the click** (Purpose B only) | **The click identifier value is not stored on any medium**: it is used on the fly for deduplication (ephemeral fingerprint ≤2 h) and only the network type is retained for attribution purposes |
| Conversion (Purpose B) | Type, amount, Client-defined properties | |

**Data the Service does NOT store**: IP addresses in the analytics database (see the "IP address" row); raw user agent; **click identifier values** (gclid, fbclid and analogues — only the network type); cookies or any terminal-equipment storage; names, emails or other direct visitor identifiers; special categories (Art. 9); identifiers capable of tracking across sites of different controllers or across different days.

### A1.3 Operations

Collection (pixel) → server-side validation and enrichment (EU) → message queue → aggregation and insertion → storage with automatic TTL → dashboard/API querying → optionally: AI insights over aggregates (Seal AI, EU) and Client-directed exports.

### A1.4 Retention periods (enforced by automatic TTL)

| Data | Period |
|------|--------|
| Event-level technical log (full URLs; no raw user agent) | **1 day** |
| Hourly aggregates | 90 days |
| Daily aggregates, conversions and their properties | **24 months** |
| Session state (operational memory) | 2 hours |
| Daily pseudonymization salt for the session identifier | **24 hours** (destroyed on rotation; excluded from backups) |
| Processing retry queues (failed messages) | Up to 7 days |
| Backups | **Own backups** (being implemented): daily, encrypted, without the event-level technical log or the daily salt, kept **for at most 30 days** (7 daily and 3 weekly). Infrastructure backups kept by the hosting provider are governed by its processing agreement (Annex 3) |
| Data after contract termination | Clause 4.8 (30 + 60 days) |

Within the 25-month maximum of the AEPD audience-measurement guide.

## ANNEX 2 — TECHNICAL AND ORGANISATIONAL MEASURES (Art. 32)

### Technical

| Measure | Implementation |
|---------|---------------|
| Encryption in transit | TLS 1.2+ on all communications, including AI inference |
| Encryption at rest | Application secrets (API keys and integration credentials) encrypted at application level; storage encryption in line with the hosting provider's measures |
| Structural minimisation | No IP persistence in the analytics database; no raw user agent; no click identifier values; persisted URLs cleaned of click identifiers; no cookies or terminal storage; URL parameters not parsed on the device |
| Ephemeral pseudonymization | Session identifier pseudonymized server-side (HMAC with a secret key + a random daily salt destroyed on rotation and excluded from backups): not recomputable by third parties and not linkable across days or across sites |
| Aggregation threshold | Minimum aggregation threshold (k≥10) in reports, with an "Aggregated" category consistent with the totals — *planned; until implemented, reports are not described as anonymous* |
| Isolation | Per-client logical separation across all tables and keys |
| Automatic retention | Database-level TTL (A1.4), not dependent on manual processes |
| Access control | RBAC, MFA for personnel, least privilege, logged access |
| Secrets management | Platform keys kept outside the code repository, in restricted-access environment configuration; content logging verifiably prohibited across the AI chain |
| Supply-chain hardening | Dependency install scripts blocked with an allowlist |
| Backups | Being implemented: asymmetric encryption before each backup is written (the private key is not on Sealmetrics' servers); copy outside the main server in dedicated storage within the EU (Annex 3); restricted access; quarterly restore test; deletions already carried out are re-applied after any restore |
| Monitoring | Security metrics and alerts; administration logging |

### Organisational

Privacy training; confidentiality undertakings; documented breach-management procedure (with the timing of clause 4.5); rights procedure; due diligence and Art. 28 contracts with all sub-processors; periodic internal audit of technical-legal compliance (the assessment of clause 3.5).

Current public list: **https://sealmetrics.com/dpa** (change-notification mechanism per clause 4.3).

## ANNEX 4 — TRANSFER FRAMEWORK (conditional)

In the standard Service flow **there are no transfers outside the EEA of visitor data** (clause 7.1), so this annex only operates if a non-EEA sub-processor were engaged in the future: SCCs under Decision 2021/914, Module 3 (processor→sub-processor) or the applicable module; Clause 9 under general authorisation with list; Spanish governing law; AEPD as reference authority; SCC Annexes I and II completed by reference to Annexes 1 and 2 of this DPA; a transfer impact assessment documented before engagement.
